Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: While specific numerical values in the plan deviate by 3-20% from actual results (e.g., past tense token lens claimed ~65% but actual is 85.4%), the main qualitative conclusions match the data: concept lens is best for semantic tasks (capital cities 83.4%, family 51.6%), token lens is best for grammatical tasks (present participle 68.3%, past tense 85.4%), and both outperform raw hidden states and all-heads baselines. The directional conclusions are supported by the evidence.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All methodology steps from the plan are fully implemented: (1) OV matrix construction via get_ov_sum(), (2) word embedding extraction via proj_onto_ov(), (3) parallelogram arithmetic via get_parallelogram_scores(), (4) four settings comparison in all_parallelograms.py, (5) effective rank analysis in parallelogram_ranks.py. All 14 word2vec tasks and 27 FV tasks are run across layers [0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,31] with k=80 heads as specified.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: The reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitude: concept lens achieves 83.4% on capital cities (38x random baseline, +36.8% over raw), family 51.6% (24x random, +23.5% over raw). Token lens achieves 68.3% on present participle (45x random, +38.2% over raw) and 85.4% on past tense (68x random, +53.5% over raw). All effects show 10-68x improvement over random chance and 16-52 percentage point absolute improvements.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: Multiple key design choices lack explicit justification: (1) k=80 heads is not justified, (2) layer selection stride of 4 is not explained, (3) cosine similarity for nearest neighbor is not justified over alternatives. Additionally, intermediate conclusions are based on mixed evidence - family task achieves only 51.6% and present participle only 68.3%, both below the 80% causal test threshold. The rank-256 performance claim only holds for some tasks (capital cities retains ~100%, but gram5/7 drop to 66-68%).
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Results are reported as single point estimates without uncertainty quantification. No error bars or confidence intervals are shown in figures. No statistical tests (t-tests, bootstrap, etc.) are performed to compare methods. No standard deviations or standard errors are reported. While individual per-example scores are saved, no aggregated uncertainty measures appear in the documentation or visualizations.
